_meta.method: Each value is Stata's own r() result read right after the command in its cmd field, as a double. Percentiles are _pctile's (the rule summarize, detail uses); mean, sum, min, max, sd and count summarize's; var and skewness summarize, detail's; cv r(sd)/r(mean); iqr _pctile p(75) - p(25); dcount the number of groups egen group() forms. rule_cases: _pctile x on x = 1..n, so an integer result j is x_(j) and j + 0.5 the mean of x_(j) and x_(j+1).
_meta.percentile_rule: Measured over 1,643,898 cases (n = 1..300 and 12 larger n up to 1e6 on every p of one and two decimals, 1,296 p one ulp at a time either side of an exact-integer n*p/100, and 126 more): P = n*p/100 in double; if |P - round(P)| <= 1e-15 * P, P is an integer and the percentile is (x_(P) + x_(P+1))/2, clamped to x_(1) and x_(n); otherwise it is x_(ceil(P)). p must be greater than 0 and less than 100 (_pctile: percentiles must be between 0 and 100, r(198), for 0 and 100 themselves).
_meta.rule_cases_selection: the 1,947 (n, p) of the one- and two-decimal grid where the absolute 1e-12 rule dash used before WP-23 disagreed with Stata, 1,500 grid rows where it agreed (Python random.seed(20260923)), every ulp probe and every discriminating probe; this generator keeps those (n, p) and re-measures each result
_meta.scopes: all: no qualifier; f1/f0: if foreign==1/0; in50: in 1/50; rng: if inrange(weight, 2000, 3500) (a range filter); sld: if mpg >= 22 (a slider filter); f0rng, in50sld: the two combined; in30: in 1/30 (a brush of the first 30 rows); f1in30: if foreign==1 in 1/30; empty: if foreign==0 & foreign==1; one: if mpg >= 22 in 1/1
